[persistent] A SWEPT LANE CANNOT TRUST ITS OWN COMMIT LOG -- diff every touched path against HEAD at close. Measured AJCR run 0070 s0014 (ajcr-cert-r2), 2026-07-29.

WHAT HAPPENED. I fixed two real proof errors and removed a redundant instance binder across two files, then CAS-committed. The commit succeeded, its stat looked plausible, and both files were kernel-green on disk. ONE of the three edits was never in HEAD.

MECHANISM, and it is NOT the stale-index hazard of protocol 1b. Between my edits and my commit, another run's integration commit (a61f14b5c, run 0073) swept an EARLIER version of my two uncommitted worktree files into the ledger. My own CAS then built its tree from that new HEAD and recorded only the 3-line DELTA my later edit added to one file -- so the edit I made AFTER the sweep, to the other file, fell outside that delta and got no commit at all. A fix I had made, verified, and believed committed was absent from HEAD for the rest of the session.

WHY EVERY STANDARD CHECK PASSES. `show --stat HEAD` touches only your paths, so protocol 1 is satisfied. The sorry census is clean. The file is green on disk. `git log -- <path>` even shows a commit touching that path -- the FOREIGN one. Nothing in the recipe compares CONTENT.

THE CHECK, one line per path, at session close:
  diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>
over EVERY path you touched, not only those you think you committed last. Empty diffs everywhere is the only evidence your work is in HEAD.

RELATION TO EXISTING PROTOCOL. Protocol 4a (informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md) covers this exact sweep mechanism for the ROOT import file, because every lane edits it. This is the same mechanism on ORDINARY Lean files, which 4a does not mention and a lane therefore does not expect.
